# Leslie Moore

## Overview

- **Age:** Twenty-eight  <sub>[v4 c13 P15](../source/v04-c13.md#nw-v04-c13-p0015)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v4 c10 P6](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0006), [v4 c10 P10](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0010)</sub>
- **Status:** Widow, engaged to Owen Ford  <sub>[v4 c31 P28](../source/v04-c31.md#nw-v04-c31-p0028), [v4 c32 P3](../source/v04-c32.md#nw-v04-c32-p0003), [v4 c38 P10](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0010)</sub>
- **Origin:** Four Winds  <sub>[v4 c11 P15](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0015)</sub>

## Appearance

Leslie is an exceptionally beautiful woman with a fine figure, an ivory-tinted complexion, and vibrant hair that gleams like molten gold or flame. She has unique eyes—one sea-blue and one hazel—which she inherited as a family trait. She habitually wears a touch of crimson on her clothing, such as a red scarf, flower, or girdle, to satisfy her inner craving for color.

_Sources: [v4 c10 P28](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0028), [v4 c11 P15](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0015), [v4 c12 P5](../source/v04-c12.md#nw-v04-c12-p0005), [v4 c13 P15](../source/v04-c13.md#nw-v04-c13-p0015), [v4 c23 P24](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0024), [v4 c38 P1](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0001), [v4 c38 P5](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0005)_

## Personality

Intelligent, spirited, and fiercely independent, Leslie carries intense pride alongside deep emotional scars. Though naturally warm, witty, and eager for life, years of trauma and tragic isolation left her guarded, cold, and prone to bitter or sullen spells. She is intensely loyal and devoted to her loved ones, willing to sacrifice her own happiness for their protection. When surrounded by understanding friends, her vibrant, joyful, and brilliant nature resurfaces.

## History

Leslie West grew up in Four Winds amidst financial struggles and family tragedies, losing her brother Kenneth and discovering her father after he committed suicide. She excelled academically at Queen's Academy with dreams of attending Redmond College, but sacrificed her ambitions when her mother begged her to marry Dick Moore to save their mortgaged farm. Shortly after their marriage, Dick left on a sea voyage; twelve years later, Captain Jim brought back an amnesiac imbecile believed to be Dick, whom Leslie faithfully nursed in near-poverty for eleven years. Upon meeting Anne Blythe, Leslie gradually let down her defensive barriers and formed a deep, emotional friendship, though she struggled with jealousy over Anne's happy life. When writer Owen Ford stayed as her summer boarder, they fell in love, which plunged Leslie into anguish over her marital trap. Dr. Gilbert Blythe eventually persuaded Leslie to send her husband to Montreal for a trephining operation; the procedure restored his memory, revealing that he was actually Dick's double-cousin, George Moore, and that Dick had died of yellow fever years prior in Cuba. Freed from her burden, Leslie returned home and accepted Owen Ford's proposal of marriage.

## Background by volume

- Daughter of Frank West and Rose Elliott West  <sub>[v4 c11 P15](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0015)</sub>
- Had a younger brother, Kenneth, who was tragically killed in a childhood accident  <sub>[v4 c11 P15](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0015), [v4 c21 P39](../source/v04-c21.md#nw-v04-c21-p0039), [v4 c21 P41](../source/v04-c21.md#nw-v04-c21-p0041)</sub>
- Discovered her father's body after he committed suicide when she was fourteen  <sub>[v4 c11 P20](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0020)</sub>
- Earned a First-Class teacher's license at Queen's Academy in a single year  <sub>[v4 c11 P22](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0022)</sub>
- Forced into marriage with Dick Moore to prevent the loss of her mother's home  <sub>[v4 c11 P26](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0026), [v4 c11 P27](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0027)</sub>

## Quotes

> I am Leslie Moore—Mrs. Dick Moore  <sub>[v4 c10 P10](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0010)</sub>

> I had a house of dreams once—but it was a palace  <sub>[v4 c10 P27](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0027)</sub>

> I suppose I am beautiful. I hate my beauty. I wish I had always been as brown and plain as the brownest and plainest girl at the fishing village over there.  <sub>[v4 c10 P31](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0031)</sub>

> Anne, there have been times this past winter and spring when I have HATED you.  <sub>[v4 c21 P5](../source/v04-c21.md#nw-v04-c21-p0005)</sub>

> I love the red roses. Anne likes the pink ones best, and Gilbert likes the white. But I want the crimson ones. They satisfy some craving in me as no other flower does.  <sub>[v4 c38 P5](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0005)</sub>
